topics.flagship-ru-ua: Libyan officials say a suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship at a naval base in Libya, the day's most widely carried story (7 outlets). Zelenskyy urged the US to release Patriot missiles after Russian drones killed at least two people near Kyiv and shelling killed one in Zaporizhzhia. Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper, and Denmark expelled a Russian official over an alleged plot on Danish soil. A rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, and a single outlet reports 'Ukrainian' drones hit the cargo ship Sparta II, believed to carry military equipment, in the Baltic. Another single-source report of Russian missiles hitting Poland is unverified.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Israeli air strikes continue in Gaza, and displaced Palestinians are protesting; a Gaza mayor describes the destruction of residential buildings as a 'gradual displacement' policy. In the Gulf, Bahrain accuses Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility, two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran's IRGC says it downed a US drone. Iran says Hormuz can reopen if the US accepts its conditions, and it unveiled an underground 'missile city' with a new double launcher. The US has added sanctions and keeps its naval blockade. Trump reportedly said he is weighing renewed major strikes on Iran in 2027, per a single outlet.
topics.T15: Central Florida is dealing with historic flooding, with evacuation alerts along the St. Johns River, while floodwaters are receding in parts of Volusia County and leaving costly cleanup. Other items are recovery or preparedness stories: Peru and Colombia after earthquakes, a cyclone evacuation in Ganjam, India, and Nepal climate-financing commentary. No major new access-denial event stands out.
topics.T01: Drone attacks near Sudan's capital killed four and damaged a UN building and Khartoum's airport, with the Rapid Support Forces blamed. In Yemen, Houthi media report an airstrike on a telecom facility in Hodeidah that killed four, and Houthi-aligned outlets accuse Saudi forces of strikes on communications networks in Saada, Taiz and Hajjah. These are partisan, single-source claims. Other items include South Korea's commemoration of the 2010 shelling of Yeonpyeong and a report on Burma's junta pressuring migrant workers to fund its war.
topics.T02: Aid cuts and the approach of winter threaten displaced families in Darfur, and Sudan's displaced elderly face particular hardship. Haiti's farmers are struggling with gang violence, hunger and El Niño, and a separate report warns a 'super El Niño' will worsen global hunger alongside war and aid cuts. Afghanistan's projected growth is not improving household incomes. Human Rights Watch reports the World Court found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya.
topics.T03: A single outlet reports that the US intelligence behind CNN's claim of an Iranian dirty-bomb or chemical plot against senior US officials originated with Israel, citing a New York Times report. Trump said the US is 'looking into it', while Rubio saw no imminent threat and Iran's foreign minister called the claims 'rubbish'. The account is polemical and the underlying intelligence is unverified. A separate item covers a biotech CEO urging a bioweapon-style approach to fentanyl.
topics.T04: Diphtheria deaths in Nigeria have reached 406 in seven months according to MSF, and experts are calling for booster doses and wider child immunisation. Malawi has introduced strict border checks and quarantine to keep Ebola out.
topics.T05: Israel's Eisenkot-led opposition bloc is setting up committees to draft bills reversing Netanyahu-era judicial changes, while Bennett warns that a government dependent on Arab-party votes could ignite mass protests. Former Brazilian president Bolsonaro was reportedly hospitalised with severe abdominal pain, but the item has no corroborating sources. The remaining stories are opinion or sparse, and no clear coup indicator appears.
topics.T06: Bangladesh's former health secretary was jailed after a 3-day remand in a July Uprising murder case, the best-sourced item here (3 outlets). Other items are mostly opinion calling for protests or strikes in Europe and the UK, plus a US tycoon released on bail in Spain over anti-Israel riots. No sign of regime-threatening unrest emerges.
topics.T07: Kim Jong Un is reportedly ignoring Trump's attempts at contact while North Korea expands a nuclear arsenal capable of reaching US cities (3 outlets). Kim also said Pyongyang seeks no regional dominance and defends its buildup as self-defense. A senior Iranian general questioned whether Khamenei's fatwa on nuclear weapons could change. A single opinion piece claims the Chinese, Russian and US presidents met in Shenzhen and issued a peace declaration, which is unconfirmed here.
topics.T08: Hyderabad police stepped up security after an email threatened a 26/11-style attack to avenge a killed militant. In Nigeria, the military says air strikes killed 21 ISWAP fighters in Borno, and a village head and his family were killed in an attack in Niger State. Ecuador's president reportedly declared an 'internal armed conflict' after the apparent escape of Los Choneros leader Adolfo Macias.
topics.T10: A CBO report estimates Trump's proposed 15 nuclear-powered battleships would cost $275 billion, $118 billion above the Navy's estimate. UN talks in Geneva failed to produce binding rules on autonomous weapons, and Australia dismissed a US report that AUKUS could weaken the US Navy. Greece and Israel are discussing roughly €1 billion in defense deals, and Kim Jong Un defended North Korea's arms buildup as self-defense.
topics.T11: Two Indian Army soldiers were killed when a tank ran over them during an exercise in Haryana, the most widely carried item (8 outlets). Polish special forces reportedly evaded US forces and drones in NATO's Deep Strike exercise. India and Nepal will hold the 20th Suryakiran exercise, and the Nigerian Army is starting Exercise Mugun Bugu V in Oyo. A blackout drill in Kanpur was also reported.
topics.T12: A suspected breach of the FBI's National Crime Information Center has drawn warnings that altered records could endanger police at traffic stops (5 outlets). The US also saw a Delta weight-and-balance outage reportedly delaying about 3,500 flights, and a Microsoft 365 outage lasting nearly 24 hours that Microsoft attributes to a dormant networking bug. DNI Jay Clayton warned of 'bumps in the road' ahead of Thanksgiving travel. Separately, hackers accessed Austrian Foreign Ministry staff contact data, and Optimizely-linked malware reportedly hit 178 organizations.
topics.T13: Spanish police report that 10,000 identical inflatables were handed out before a mass crossing of about 80,000 Moroccans into Ceuta on July 30-31, which they believe was coordinated. Other items are opinion-heavy: English villages facing asylum housing and a conservative critique of Democratic immigration bills. Coverage is thin and partisan.
topics.T16: House Democrats clinched at least 258 seats, their largest majority since 1992 (3 outlets). Flavio Bolsonaro alleges Brazil's Supreme Court ordered his passport seized minutes after his election loss, per a single outlet. Israel's coalition talks continue after an inconclusive October election, and Trump floated Stephen Miller as a 2028 candidate. Other items cover Nigeria's 2027 race, an Indian voter roll revision and an Alberta referendum analysis.

bluf: A Russian warship was reportedly struck by suspected Ukrainian drones at a naval base in Libya, according to Libyan officials and 7 outlets, a possible extension of the Ukraine war beyond Europe. Zelenskyy is urging the US to release Patriot missiles after Russian drone and shelling attacks killed three people near Kyiv and in Zaporizhzhia. Poland says Russia twice tried to kill a Ukrainian American rapper, and Denmark expelled a Russian official over an alleged assassination plot on Danish soil. In Gaza, Israeli strikes continue and a local mayor describes a policy of 'gradual displacement', while displaced Palestinians protest. In US politics, Democrats secured at least 258 House seats, the largest majority since 1992. Separately, a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, and a single outlet reportedly says drones hit the cargo ship Sparta II in the Baltic while it was bound for the enclave. In the Gulf, two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz, Bahrain accuses Iran of striking a civilian facility, and Iran says it downed a US drone while US sanctions and the blockade continue.
